entries.title: I Corinthians 13:1
segments: ¶Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:2
segments: And though I have [the gift of] prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:3
segments: And though I bestow all my goods to feed [the poor], and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:4
segments: ¶Love suffers long [and] is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up;

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:5
segments: does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil;

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:6
segments: does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth;

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:7
segments: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:8
segments: ¶Love never fails. But whether [there are] prophecies, they will fail; whether [there are] tongues, they will cease; whether [there is] knowledge, it will vanish away.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:9
segments: For we know in part and we prophesy in part.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:10
segments: But when that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part will be done away.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:11
segments: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:12
segments: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I also am known.

entries.title: I Corinthians 13:13
segments: And now abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these [is] love.
